chapter: Imperial Orchestra and Southern Rhythm Boys
title: Women instrumentalists and Jeanette Kimball
summary: Asked about women in bands, she names pianist Jeanette Kimball of Papa Celestin's orchestra and her guitarist husband.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: We talked before about women with bands and I asked you wasn't it rather unusual for you, especially at your age, to be playing with a band, and you mentioned that there were several women around New Orleans. You named one, Jeanette Kimball. You said she was with --
Papa Celestin, , right. She was marvelous, marvelous pianist.
That you can remember the names of.

Offhand I -- isn't it funny, I can't think of any other names right now, but Jeanette was outstanding, because she was with Papa Celestin. Her husband at that time was also with the orchestra. He was a marvelous guitar player.

What is it? Kimball. Kimball. I can't think of his first name now, but he is right now working in New Orleans with the -- at the Preservation Band, I think. A guitarist. But he and Jeannette -- well Jeannette, as I say,
she was just a marvelous pianist, and she was with Papa Celestin's orchestra oh, for quite awhile.
